questions.question: Explain the main causes of the frontier wars on the eastern frontier.
questions.expected_answer: Competition for land (main cause; each war ended with colonial land gains); cattle raiding and the commando/reprisal system (seizing cattle from the nearest homestead); different ideas of land and borders (fixed lines vs communal, flexible allocation); aggressive colonial policy (1812 Zuurveld expulsion, buffer zones, annexation); rivalries between Xhosa chiefs (Ngqika vs Ndlambe) exploited by the colony; drought and population pressure; missionaries and prophets (Makhanda, Mlanjeni).

questions.question: Describe the fifth and sixth frontier wars.
questions.expected_answer: Fifth (1818-1819): British support for Ngqika against Ndlambe; Ndlambe won at Amalinde (1818); British attacked Ndlambe; prophet Makhanda led 6000-10 000 warriors against Grahamstown on 22 April 1819, defeated by a few hundred soldiers with Khoikhoi marksmen and cannon; Makhanda surrendered, was imprisoned on Robben Island and drowned escaping (1820); Ceded Territory between Fish and Keiskamma. Sixth (1834-1835): Xhosa under Maqoma and Tyhali invaded after a chief was shot and land losses; D'Urban and Harry Smith invaded Xhosa land; Hintsa held and shot dead (1835), body mutilated; Queen Adelaide Province annexed but returned in 1836.

questions.question: What were the consequences of the frontier wars?
questions.expected_answer: For the Xhosa: loss of most land to colonial farms; loss of hundreds of thousands of cattle; many killed and many more died of hunger and displacement (worsened by the cattle-killing of 1856-57); chiefs replaced by colonial magistrates; many forced into wage labour on farms and later mines; society disrupted; independence ended by 1879. For the colony: land gained but huge costs and long insecurity. Today remembered as wars of resistance and dispossession.
